name: Word Rarity Score
description: Evaluates the document based on the frequency of 'rare' or 'archaic' vocabulary. Large Language Models (LLMs) are optimized to output the most probable sequences of tokens based on their massive training datasets. Consequently, they tend to favor common, high-probability words and actively avoid lexical outliers—words that are rarely used in modern, everyday language. Human writers, however, frequently employ rare, domain-specific, or slightly archaic words to add color, precision, or personal voice to their writing. This algorithm measures the concentration of these low-probability 'long-tail' words. A lack of rare words is a strong indicator of the artificial smoothing typical of generative AI.
mechanism: The algorithm cross-references every token in the text against a comprehensive frequency dictionary of the target language. Words are categorized into frequency bands. The system specifically scans for words that fall into the lowest probability percentiles (the 'long tail' of the Zipfian distribution). It then calculates a global 'Rarity Score' based on the density and distribution of these unusual terms. AI-generated text typically registers a disproportionately low Rarity Score, heavily localized around the top 5,000 most common words. Human text features periodic 'spikes' into the extreme tail end of the vocabulary distribution.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing academic papers, creative writing, literature reviews, and opinion pieces where human authors typically utilize a broad and specialized vocabulary. It is particularly useful for detecting 'bland' AI writing that lacks distinct authorial voice.
strengths:
• Excellent at differentiating between a human expert's nuanced vocabulary and an LLM's generic, safe word choices.
• Highly effective against standard prompt generation without complex vocabulary parameter tuning.
limitations:
• Vulnerable to specific prompt engineering techniques where the user commands the AI to 'use rare words', 'write in an archaic style', or 'use advanced vocabulary'.
• May yield false positives on texts intentionally written in 'Plain English' or domains requiring strictly standardized, simple terminology (e.g., basic instructions, children's literature).
parameters:
Analysis: Long-Tail Vocabulary Distribution
Metrics: Density of Low-Frequency Tokens (< 0.001% occurrence rate)
Output: 0-100 Lexical Rarity & Smoothing Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy. It is highly predictive when combined with structural metrics like Burstiness, as AI prompted to use 'rare words' often injects them awkwardly, destroying semantic coherence while boosting the rarity score.

references.title: Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL.
